title: Melissa: the virus that jammed email

scenes.narration: [serious] In 1999, one email jammed the mail at over 300 workplaces.
It started with a file shared online. It promised free passwords to adult websites.
When someone opened it, a hidden program woke up. It sent itself to their first 50 contacts.
The email said Important Message From, and a friend's name. So people trusted it, and opened it too.
About one million email accounts were hit. Fixing it cost about 80 million dollars.
Then a tip from AOL led police to one man, David Smith.
He went to prison for 20 months. The real trick was a friend's name.

facts.claim: Melissa began spreading on March 26, 1999; David Lee Smith posted the file to an internet newsgroup from a hijacked AOL account, promising passwords to adult websites
When opened in Microsoft Word, a macro sent the virus via Outlook to the first 50 contacts in the user's mailing lists
Email servers at more than 300 organizations were overloaded or shut down, about one million email accounts were disrupted, and repairs cost an estimated $80 million
A tip from AOL helped the FBI and New Jersey law enforcement trace the virus; Smith was arrested on April 1, 1999 in New Jersey, pleaded guilty in December 1999
The email subject line was 'Important Message From [name]' and the body said 'Here is that document you asked for...don't show anyone else'
On May 1, 2002 Smith was sentenced to 20 months in federal prison and a $5,000 fine; both sides agreed damage exceeded $80 million
